figures.alt: Photo of dark storm clouds over Lake Michigan with a curtain of rain falling in the distance and a sandy beach in front.
figures.caption: A storm is weather. Weather is what happens on one day.

figures.alt: Photo of a Michigan lakeside park in July with green leafy trees, a bench and blue sky.
figures.caption: July in Michigan: warm and green.

figures.alt: Photo of a Michigan lakeside park in January with snow on the ground and trees and ice along the shore.
figures.caption: January in Michigan: cold, with snow and ice. Seasons make a climate pattern.

figures.alt: Interactive: a bar graph of Detroit’s typical daily high by month with a month picker and a note that a high is not the whole-day average.
figures.caption: Pick a month to read Detroit’s typical daily high.

figures.alt: Bar graph of typical average daily high temperature in Detroit by month, in degrees Fahrenheit (°F). Jan 32, Feb 35, Mar 45, Apr 58, May 69, Jun 79, Jul 83, Aug 81, Sep 74, Oct 62, Nov 50, Dec 38. Summer months are tall, winter months are short.
figures.caption: Typical average daily HIGH temperature by month for Detroit, in °F, rounded to the nearest degree. A given year can differ by several degrees. July is the warmest at 83°F (28°C) and January the coldest at 32°F (0°C).

figures.alt: Three kids and a teacher around a table with a tilted tray: soil at the top, a grass strip at the bottom, and one child pouring water slowly from a cup.
figures.caption: A flood-barrier test: the same amount of water each time, then compare how much soil moves.

figures.alt: Bar graph of typical precipitation in Detroit by month, in inches. Jan 2, Feb 1.9, Mar 2.4, Apr 3, May 3, Jun 3.2, Jul 3.1, Aug 3.2, Sep 3, Oct 2.6, Nov 2.7, Dec 2.2. Every month is between about 1.9 inches (5 cm) and 3.2 inches (8 cm).
figures.caption: Typical precipitation by month for Detroit, in inches. It is fairly even through the year, from about 1.9 inches (5 cm) in February to 3.2 inches (8 cm) in June and August.

figures.alt: Bar graph, Sediment moved by flood water. No barrier 8 spoonfuls, Cardboard fence 5 spoonfuls, Grass model 2 spoonfuls.
figures.caption: Spoonfuls of sediment moved: no barrier 8, cardboard fence 5, grass model 2.
